stem: The number of absences by girls from a certain class on any day is modelled by a random variable with distribution $\text{Po}(0.2)$. The number of absences by boys from the same class on any day is modelled by an independent random variable with distribution $\text{Po}(0.3)$.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Find the probability that, during a randomly chosen 2-day period, the total number of absences is less than 3.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Find the probability that, during a randomly chosen 5-day period, the number of absences by boys is more than 3.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: The teacher claims that, during the football season, there are more absences by boys than usual. In order to test this claim at the 5% significance level, he notes the number of absences by boys during a randomly chosen 5-day period during the football season.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by a Type I error in this context.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State appropriate null and alternative hypotheses and find the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: In fact there were 4 absences by boys during this period. Test the teacher’s claim at the 5% significance level.
